# Deep PTC mode

1.7.3 实测汇总 / Test summary
**Reports. Asks. Stays awake. Plans. Stays reachable.**
**Five basics, one
mode; everything is a plugin, with the official preset always as the fallback.**
Deep PTC is not another tool bundle. It is a DeepSeek Harness agent preset built around five basic p
roblems in model work: working silently without reporting, guessing instead of asking when intent is
ambiguous, sleeping and becoming unreachable during a task, not planning or not showing the plan, a
nd not using the original PTC preset's concise context plus its unlimited-token prompt.
Those five are handled first by prompts and code. On top of that, following DSH's “everything is a p
lugin” philosophy, the preset adds dynamic preset/tool loading, creative-mode tools for building DSH
plugins, dsh-go screen-control adaptation, wider shell support, external plugin tool/workflow adapt
ation, and a leaner skill/tool loading flow. Deep PTC adds no task tools itself; it provides the int
erface that lets a plugin's new tools be discovered, loaded and called.
Not every third-party plugin is guaranteed to fit: the interface is verified for dsh-ops and reused
by other plugins, but a plugin still has to support the installed host and publish its tools under t
he expected contract.
## Five basic problems
| # | Problem | What Deep PTC does |
| 1 | **Working silently without reporting** | One sentence before every `run_code`; a longer update
at milestones; never more than two or three silent tool calls; a short final result with failed too

ls and providers. |
| 2 | **Guessing instead of asking** | Meaning belongs to the user, facts to the
tools: ask one to three questions with options when names, targets, routes, scope or acceptance cri

teria are unclear; look up inspectable facts yourself. The user's answer wins. |
| 3 | **Sleeping or
becoming unreachable** | Enforced in code: foreground waits move to the background after 30 s; a us
er message hands the waiting command to the background within about 2 s; foreground sleeps over 5 s

are refused; job completion wakes the model. |
| 4 | **No plan, or an invisible plan** | Plan by est
imated size: act silently under 5 minutes; show the plan and start without approval for 5–20 minutes
; show it and wait for approval over 20 minutes. Re-plan when the estimate moves up; the user can re

direct at any step. |
| 5 | **Not using the concise context and unlimited-token prompt** | Derive fr
om the live official PTC composition, keep the tool catalog compact and load full schemas on demand,
and state that this mode spends its token budget on reads, searches, commands and checks rather tha
n rationing them. The prompt does not change billing or the real token limit. |
## Built for “everything is a plugin”
### 1. Dynamic preset and tool loading
Read the running host's official PTC declaration and inherit its rows as they are; only the persona,
execution group, reachability guard, job wrapper and question wrapper are replaced. Rebuild only wh
en the declaration or settings change (checked every five seconds); fall back to the bundled snapsho
t with a warning if it cannot be loaded, parsed or derived. An official upgrade can add tools withou
t a release of this preset; existing sessions are not forcibly switched.
### 2. Flexible creative-mode tools
The plugin lab is off by default. When enabled, it reads the host's creative preset and appends only
the rows that mode adds, specifically for building DSH plugins. Module names stay as declared; skil
l directories resolve relative to the creative preset file. Lab packages stay in process memory, are
not written to the repository, shipped presets, desktop composition or this plugin's source, and ru
n only through the host's existing approval. Loading reads the roster and documents only; it never c
alls `composedPreset`.

## Compatibility and development
Deep PTC is composed at load time from the PTC preset the installed Harness declares (`@deepseek-ai/
dsh-web-app/presets/ptc.patch.yml`). Every official row is inherited as-is; Deep PTC replaces only i
ts persona text, swaps the two platform-switched shell tools for one isolated execution group, adds
the reachability guard, and wraps the official job and question tools. The wrappers and the executio
n group never name an official module themselves: they load the module the official row names (and t
he shell executors the base deployment declares in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-base/cordis.patch.yml`), with t
he official options. An official PTC change therefore reaches this mode without a plugin release, an
d a removed or renamed upstream module cannot leave a stale row behind. When the chosen execution en
vironment cannot be mapped onto the official rows, those rows are kept and the change is logged. If
the declaration cannot be resolved, read or parsed, the bundled `lib/preset.json` snapshot is used a
s a fallback and the fallback is logged.
Because the declarations are resolved through the host runtime, every host package the plugin import
s statically is declared in `peerDependencies` — including `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app`. The host rout
es those names to the installation for a linked plugin; `npm run check` fails if one is missing, whi
ch is what keeps a `link:` installation on the live declaration instead of silently using the fallba
ck snapshot. `compatibility.json` records the upstream release the checked fixture was taken from an
d its hash; `npm run check` verifies that the bundled fallback still derives the same preset as that
fixture and that the inheritance invariants hold. The engines range is an installation floor, not p
roof that every future release was tested, so run `npm run check:upstream -- <path>` against a new r
elease before trusting it.
